accept.why: esm-spec 4.8.1 registry addition: the international foot, exact at 0.3048 m. FF10 STKHGT/STKDIAM are stored in it.
FF10 STKVEL. `ft` composes like any other table symbol.
esm-spec 4.8.1 registry addition: exactly 2000 international pounds. NOT spelled `ton`.
The FF10 ANN_VALUE column's unit. The scale is exactly InMAP's 907184740000 ug / (3600*8760 s) emission-conversion constant divided by 1e9.
esm-spec 4.8.1 registry addition: the metric ton, 1000 kg. Present so the short/metric choice is one a document MAKES.
Control: the spelling `short_ton/yr` replaced in isrm.esm. Same dimension, different scale by 907.18474 -- which is exactly why the wrong one is invisible to a dimensional checker.
The concentration unit of the whole air-quality corpus.
SOLIDUS ASSOCIATIVITY (4.8.2): `/` is left-to-right, so this is (ug/m^3)/(kg/yr) and the parenthesised denominator is REQUIRED.

RATIONAL EXPONENT in its only unambiguous spelling. `(m/s)^-1/3` -- the spelling isrm.esm carried -- is a DIFFERENT string: the grammar reads it as ((m/s)^-1)/3, a scaling factor, and the three bindings disagreed about what that means.
DECIMAL exponent: the intensity of a Wiener noise term.
COUNTS ARE DIMENSIONLESS: a number density is [length]^-3, never [substance].
`%` must lex as a symbol token even though it is not alphanumeric.
The Dobson unit: dimension m^-2, scale EXACTLY 2.6867e20.
The steradian is the angle axis SQUARED, not a ninth axis.
The JULIAN year, 31557600 s exactly (365.25 days). Pinned because one binding shipped a 365-day year -- 0.0685% short, and INVISIBLE to dimensional analysis, which sees [time] either way.
The same value in the composition the ecological fixtures use.

esm-spec 4.8.1 registry addition: the international mile, EXACTLY 5280 ft = 1609.344 m by the 1959 agreement. EPA MOVES stores link.linkLength in it and its whole activity model is vehicle-MILES travelled.

link.linkAvgSpeed and driveSchedule.averageSpeed. It COMPOSES from `mi` and `h` and is not a table entry; 0.44704 is exactly the constant MOVES's own SQL writes three times in one statement. `mph` is a reject, below.
The MOVES air-toxics distance-rate output (`g/mile`). Pins that the mile composes in a DENOMINATOR too.

esm-spec 4.8.1 registry addition: the international avoirdupois pound, EXACTLY 0.45359237 kg -- and exactly short_ton/2000, which the registry already carried. MOVES tabulates brake-specific fuel consumption in lb/(hp*h).

esm-spec 4.8.1 registry addition: MECHANICAL horsepower, 550 ft*lbf/s = 745.6998715822702 W (NIST SP 811 App. B). The scale is the whole contract here: the metric horsepower (PS) is 735.49875 W, same dimension, 1.4% apart, and no dimension-only check can tell them apart. nrsourceusetype.hpAvg is the axis MOVES's NONROAD model bins on.

nremissionrate.meanBaseRate -- the unit every NONROAD emission rate is tabulated in. MOVES spells it `g/hp-hr`; the hyphen is not an operator in 4.8.2, so the ESM spelling parenthesises. Composed, not a table entry.

esm-spec 4.8.1 registry addition: the US LIQUID gallon, exactly 231 in^3 = 3.785411784 L (NIST SP 811 App. B). Again the scale is the contract: the imperial gallon is 4.54609 L, 20% away and dimensionally identical.
fueltype.fuelDensity, refuelingfactors.refuelingSpillRate and the NONROAD dioxin and metal emission rates are all per US gallon.

Added to the Rust registry by fa7ffb01e (PR #238) for MOVES's County.barometricPressure and NEVER MIRRORED to the other four bindings -- precisely the drift this fixture exists to catch, and unpinned until now. Exactly 25.4 mmHg (NIST SP 811).

reject.why: AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION: short, metric and long tons are three different masses. 4.8.1 admits `short_ton` and `tonne` and neither is spelled `ton`.
The spelling isrm.esm carried before this change. Rejected everywhere, so the document had to say which ton it meant.
A plural is not an alias. `year` IS a table key; `tons` is not.
A one-letter mass symbol reads as tera- to half its readers -- excluded for the same reason `d` is.
`ft` has no long-form alias: the table grows by demonstrated need and nothing declares `foot`.
`tonne` is the spelling; there is deliberately one.
A plural is not an alias.
4.8.1 excludes a bare `d`: it reads as deci- or as a differential. The day is `day`.
4.8.2: a digit run not separated by `^` is a DIFFERENT symbol, not an implicit exponent. Write `cm^3`.
There is NO SI-prefix mechanism (4.8.1). `molec` is a table key; `kmolec` is not.

A FUSED spelling of a compound the grammar already builds. `mi/h` is the spelling, and admitting `mph` too would make one quantity have two names -- the same argument that keeps `feet` out beside `ft`.
No corpus column is stored in inches. The only inch in MOVES is a ft-to-in conversion constant, and `inHg` is its own table entry, not `in` times `Hg`. The table grows by demonstrated need.
No corpus user at all. Listed so that the imperial family's membership is a pinned fact rather than an accident of what got filed.
A plural is not an alias, exactly as `tons/year` and `feet` are not. The imperial family is symbol-only.

MOVES's own spelling of horsepower-hour, and NOT parseable: `-` is not an operator in 4.8.2, so this reads as a dangling minus. The ESM spelling is `hp*h`. Pinned because a porter transcribing a MOVES column name will try this first.

reject_scaling_factor.why: THE STRING THAT STARTED THIS. 4.8.2 reads it as ((m/s)^-1)/3 -- a SCALING FACTOR -- and the bindings gave it three different meanings (magnitude dropped / retained / whole string rejected). Now rejected everywhere, so `^(-1/3)` is the only spelling of that unit.
A numeric atom other than 1 is a scaling factor, not a unit.
Whitespace is multiplication, so this is a scaled metre.
